title: FizzBuzz
prompt:
The shop's counting game. Count from 1 to `last`. Print `Fizz` for multiples of 3, `Buzz` for multiples of 5, `FizzBuzz` for multiples of both, and the number itself for everything else.

The loop is already there. Your job is the branching inside it. Hint from Lesson A4: `n % 3 == 0` is true when 3 divides `n` exactly.
expected_output:
1
2
Fizz
4
Buzz
Fizz
7
8
Fizz
Buzz
11
Fizz
13
14
FizzBuzz
hints: The remainder `%` tells you about multiples: `n % 5 == 0` means 5 divides `n` with nothing left over.
Check the both-at-once case first. If you test for 3 first, 15 prints Fizz and never reaches FizzBuzz.
`if n % 15 == 0:` FizzBuzz, `elif n % 3 == 0:` Fizz, `elif n % 5 == 0:` Buzz, `else:` the number.
explain_after: `%` gives the remainder [py-046], so a remainder of 0 means an exact multiple. The order of the branches matters because Python runs only the first true one. Putting the FizzBuzz test first is the whole trick.
